subject: computer-science
promptStrong: Give me a challenging GCSE exam-style question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the AQA spec.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for GCSE AQA Computer Science simply, with an example and the most common mistake.
learningObjectives: CPU components and von Neumann architecture
Memory: RAM, ROM, cache and registers

questions.q: For an AND gate with inputs A and B, when is the output 1?
options: When at least one input is 1
Only when both A and B are 1
questions.explain: An AND gate outputs 1 only when every input is 1. If either input is 0 the output is 0.

questions.q: An XOR gate has inputs A = 1 and B = 1. What is the output?
questions.explain: XOR (exclusive OR) outputs 1 only when its inputs differ. With A = 1 and B = 1 the inputs are the same, so the output is 0. XOR is now on the AQA 8525 spec alongside NOT, AND and OR.

questions.q: A NOT gate is given an input of 0. What is its output?
questions.explain: A NOT gate (inverter) has a single input and outputs the opposite value, so an input of 0 gives an output of 1.

questions.q: Which of these is an example of application software?
questions.explain: Application software performs end-user tasks, e.g. a word processor. The OS, drivers and utilities are all system software that manages the computer's resources.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the management functions of an operating system listed by AQA?
questions.explain: The OS manages the processor(s), memory, I/O devices, applications and security. It does not manufacture hardware.

questions.q: Which statement about assembly language is correct?
options: It is a high-level language that is easy to read for most people
It is the same as Python
It has a one-to-one (1:1) correspondence with machine code
questions.explain: Assembly language is a low-level language with a 1:1 correspondence to machine code and is often used for embedded systems and controlling hardware.

questions.q: What does an assembler do?
options: Translates a high-level language into machine code all at once
Executes source code line by line without producing machine code
Translates assembly language into machine code, one line to one instruction
questions.explain: An assembler translates assembly language into machine code, with each line of assembly assembled into a single machine code instruction.

questions.q: How does an interpreter differ from a compiler?
options: An interpreter translates and runs the code statement by statement rather than producing a separate machine-code file first
A compiler runs the program line by line without translating it
An interpreter always produces a faster final program
questions.explain: An interpreter translates and executes the program one statement at a time and does not generate machine code directly, whereas a compiler translates the whole program into machine code before it runs.

questions.lo: CPU components and von Neumann architecture
questions.q: Which CPU component carries out arithmetic and logical operations?
questions.explain: The ALU performs arithmetic (e.g. addition) and logical operations (e.g. comparisons, AND/OR/NOT). The control unit coordinates the CPU and the clock generates timing signals.

questions.lo: CPU components and von Neumann architecture
questions.q: In the von Neumann architecture, where are both program instructions and the data they use stored?
options: In separate physical memories that can never be mixed
questions.explain: A key feature of von Neumann architecture is the stored-program concept: instructions and data share the same main memory.

questions.q: Which correctly lists the three stages of the Fetch-Execute cycle in order?
questions.explain: The CPU fetches the next instruction from main memory, decodes it to work out what it is, then executes it. This repeats continually.

questions.q: Increasing which of these would generally improve CPU performance?
questions.explain: A higher clock speed means more instructions per second. More cores and a larger cache also improve performance; lower clock speed, fewer cores and smaller cache reduce it.

questions.lo: Memory: RAM, ROM, cache and registers
questions.q: Which statement correctly describes RAM and ROM?
options: Both RAM and ROM keep their data forever
RAM is volatile and loses its contents when power is off; ROM is non-volatile
Both RAM and ROM lose their data when switched off
ROM is volatile; RAM keeps its contents without power
questions.explain: RAM is volatile, so its contents are lost when power is removed; ROM is non-volatile and retains data (often start-up instructions) with no power.

questions.q: Which is an advantage of solid state storage (SSD) over magnetic hard disk (HDD)?
options: It has no moving parts, so is faster and more shock-resistant
It is always cheaper per gigabyte
It is volatile and needs power to keep data
It always stores more data than any HDD
questions.explain: SSDs use electrical circuits and have no moving parts, making them faster, quieter and more shock-resistant. They are non-volatile; HDDs are often cheaper per gigabyte.

questions.q: How many bits are there in one byte?
questions.explain: A byte is a group of 8 bits. A bit (0 or 1) is the fundamental unit of information.

questions.q: What is the 8-bit binary number 10110110 in decimal?
questions.explain: 128 + 32 + 16 + 4 + 2 = 182. The column values 128 64 32 16 8 4 2 1 are added wherever a 1 appears.

questions.q: What is the decimal number 45 written in hexadecimal?
questions.explain: 45 = 2 x 16 + 13. 2 gives the digit 2 and 13 gives D, so 45 is 2D in hexadecimal.

questions.q: Applying a logical left shift of 2 places to a binary number is equivalent to which operation?
questions.explain: Each left shift multiplies by 2, so a shift of 2 places multiplies by 2 x 2 = 4. A logical right shift would divide by powers of 2.

questions.q: In 7-bit ASCII the character A has code 65. What is the code for D?
questions.explain: Character codes run in sequence, so B = 66, C = 67 and D = 68. Knowing the code for A lets you work out the others by counting on.

questions.q: A bitmap image is 10 pixels wide, 8 pixels high, with a colour depth of 4 bits. What is its size in bits (ignoring headers)?
questions.explain: File size in bits = width x height x colour depth = 10 x 8 x 4 = 320 bits (which is 40 bytes).
